Concentration risk can be calculated for a single bank loan or whole portfolio using a "concentration ratio". For a whole portfolio, a herfindahl index is used to calculate the degree of concentration to a single name, sector of the economy or country.
For a single loan, the concentration ratio is simply the proportion of the portfolio the loan represents. a $100 loan in a $1000 portfolio would have a ratio of 0.1 or 10%
For a single loan, the concentration ratio is simply the proportion of the portfolio the loan represents. a portfolio with 10 equally sized loans would have a concentration ratio of 0.1 or 10%

For a single loan, the concentration ratio is simply the proportion of the portfolio the loan represents. a portfolio of 10 loans - 9 equally sized and 1 equal to half the value of the portfolio would have a concentration ratio of 0.27 or 27%
Concentration risk can be calculated for a single bank loan or whole portfolio using a "concentration ratio". Separate concentration ratios must be calculated for each type of concentration.

Concentration risk can be calculated for a single bank loan or whole portfolio using a "concentration ratio". The ratio is useful for bankers or investors at large to identify when a portfolio may be excessively exposed to the risk that a recession or downturn in one sector of the economy or another country may cause a high proportion of the bank's outstanding loans to default.
mechanism: Calculating concentration risk helps identify excessive exposure, which then allows bankers/investors to mitigate potential defaults due to economic downturns.
